analysis: No new macro shock arrived over the weekend; the story is the fade of Friday's dovish repricing into Monday's premarket — futures gave back across the board while the 10Y only eased to 5.26%, and the tape now waits on Wednesday's FOMC minutes plus the Fed speaker slate (Logan's +50bp call, Hammack's 'inflationary mindset' warning). Oil is the swing macro variable with a genuinely messy weekend: a Saudi Aramco refinery attack pushed Brent above $103 even as OPEC+ left November quotas unchanged and the G7's 100M-barrel release stayed plan-stage, not barrels — the early-Monday crude relief is fragile. The AI bid is expressing itself through deals and partnerships rather than multiple expansion this morning (Qualcomm-Huawei cross-license, Altman's Cerebras reassurance, NetApp-SMCI), while semis are a two-way market: Intel's -3.2% on the Musk/Terafab/TSMC news sits against Friday's +3% INTC/AMD bid. The notable status change is Meta: the New Mexico penalty request is now Reuters-confirmed, but the stock brushed it off Thursday (+0.1%, +27% in September) — the market is pricing the AI story over the legal risk, so the judge's ruling later this month is the real catalyst, not today's ask. The two AI-finance stories (FT's Amazon $8B chip SPV, Bloomberg's Broadcom $60B Anthropic financing) remain single-source and unresolved. Noise to discount: thin 4am futures moves and the weekend oil headline whipsaw. USAC exits the NYSE Friday and debuts on the TXSE today — a venue move, not a business change.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Futures opened Monday in the red: Dow futures -97 points (-0.2%), with S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures also -0.2%, as Friday's jobs-driven rally faded. Traders price an 82% chance the Fed holds on Oct. 28 (vs 29% a week ago); the 10Y eased 3bps to 5.26% on early oil weakness (Barron's, updated <1h ago).
headlines.why_it_matters: The fade, not the rally, is the Monday tell — the dovish repricing stuck on the Fed path but yields never got a clean break; red futures into a heavy week (FOMC minutes Wed) lean growth-negative until buyers show.

headlines.headline: Friday carry: the S&P 500 rose 0.7% to 7,722.72 (within 1% of its record), the Dow added 0.5% to 51,176.96 and the Nasdaq set a record at 27,190.86 (+1.2%) after the soft September jobs print (29k vs ~84k expected, unemployment 4.2%); weekly: Dow -1.3%, S&P -0.3%, Nasdaq +0.5%. The 10Y closed at 5.28% (+4bps) after touching 5.16% post-print; VIX closed at 15.31.
headlines.why_it_matters: Classic bad-news-is-good-news that held into the close — the market read 29k payrolls as rate-hike relief (Oct hike odds ~22% Friday vs ~64% a week ago); the risk is the 10Y snapping back toward Thursday's 24-year high ~5.35%.

headlines.headline: Oil whipsawed over the weekend: WTI closed Friday at $91.11 (-1.9%) on G7 plans for a ~100M-barrel diesel-and-crude stock release, then a weekend attack on a Saudi Aramco refinery pushed Brent back above $103; OPEC+ kept November quotas unchanged Sunday, Iran is still refusing to reopen Hormuz without US concessions, and crude was lower again early Monday on the G7 plans and rising Middle East exports. Trump said the US will not impose a diesel export ban.
headlines.why_it_matters: Energy is the swing macro input this week — cheaper oil eases the bond story but the release is plan-stage, not barrels, and an attack headline can reverse it in one print; the 10Y moved 3bps on oil alone this morning.

headlines.headline: Meta's New Mexico legal overhang is now Reuters-confirmed (no longer single-source): the state asked a judge Thursday for $35-40B in privacy penalties after a Sept. 25 jury found Meta misled users in 43M+ violations of consumer-protection law; Meta called the ask 'astronomical' and seeks a $3.45B cap. Judge Francis Mathew is expected to rule later this month. META closed Thursday at $725.93 and rose 27% in September.
headlines.why_it_matters: A headline-size penalty number now on the official record — the stock shrugged it Thursday (+0.1%), so the market is pricing Meta's AI story over the legal risk; the judge's ruling later this month is the actual catalyst to watch, not today's ask.

headlines.headline: Qualcomm advanced 3.8% in premarket after the chipmaker and Huawei announced a multi-year patent license agreement including cross-licenses to their 5G, compute, AI, and networking patent portfolios (Barron's stock movers, ~1h ago).
headlines.why_it_matters: A licensing deal that reads as AI/datacom IP monetization — the kind of partnership headline that keeps the AI-infrastructure bid alive independent of the rate tape.

headlines.headline: Intel slipped 3.2% premarket after Elon Musk confirmed TSMC is in talks with his chip venture Terafab; Intel is also a Terafab partner (Barron's stock movers, ~1h ago).
headlines.why_it_matters: A foundry-partnership headline that favors TSMC in the narrative — semis are two-way this morning after Friday's INTC/AMD +3% bid, and any Terafab share shift is margin-relevant for Intel.

headlines.headline: PTC surged 35% to $194.56 after Schneider Electric agreed to buy the industrial-software maker for $205 a share in a $22.6B all-cash deal (Barron's stock movers, ~1h ago).
headlines.why_it_matters: A take-private premium this size signals acquirers are still paying up for industrial software — a sentiment read-through for enterprise-tech multiples, not just the two names.

headlines.headline: Overnight/premarket AI bid: Cerebras (CBRS) rose 7% premarket after OpenAI's Sam Altman pushed back on speculation its role was shrinking, calling Cerebras a 'close partner'; Super Micro drew retail attention on its broad AI infrastructure partnership with NetApp; Seagate and Western Digital gained on weekend buy recs after the Toshiba HDD-capacity selloff was called an overreaction.
headlines.why_it_matters: Leadership keeps broadening from semis into servers, storage and alternative-AI-chip names — the rally's legs are partnership-driven right now, which holds up better than pure multiple expansion if yields re-attack the high.

headlines.headline: Carried forward: Tesla held its Q3-deliveries beat into Friday, +5.7% to ~$367 (486,532 deliveries vs ~457-462k estimates) with no Q2-style sell-the-news; Wedbush's Dan Ives said over the weekend that Tesla's AI pivot is coming and 2027 'could be a golden year.' The two AI-finance stories (FT's Amazon $8B Nvidia-chip SPV, Bloomberg's Broadcom $60B Anthropic financing) remain single-source and unresolved.
headlines.why_it_matters: Tesla stabilized after the print — the Ives note is analyst framing, not news, so it won't move the tape alone; the two unconfirmed AI-finance stories are the actual swing factors for semis into the week.

headlines.headline: Fed counterweight over the weekend: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack warned in a PBS interview that Americans could develop an 'inflationary mindset' — businesses raising prices 'a little extra' in anticipation of inflation — and cautioned against putting too much weight on a single jobs report, characterizing the labor market as relatively stable.
headlines.why_it_matters: A hawkish-leaning speaker read after a dovish print — the Fed's own commentary is the main brake on the post-jobs rally, and Logan's +50bp call Thursday plus this make the speaker slate the week's tape-mover alongside Wednesday's minutes.

Monday premarket: futures -0.2% across the board as the post-jobs rally fades. No sourced advance/decline ratio or volume-vs-20d figures for the prior session.
market_snapshot.notes: Mon 4:00am PT premarket, post-weekend. Last regular session Friday Oct 2. 10Y 5.26% early Monday (-3bps on oil retreat) vs 5.28% Friday close (+4bps on the day, after 5.16% post-print and Thursday's 24Y high ~5.35%). CME: 82% chance Fed holds Oct 28 (vs 29% a week ago). Bitcoin $86,222 (+1.3% over 24h); crypto stocks higher (Coinbase +2.3%, Strategy +3%).

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news. Today is the TXSE debut — units begin trading on the Texas Stock Exchange under the unchanged ticker USAC; unitholders take no action. The SEC Form 25 (NYSE delisting) and 8-A12B filed over the weekend were listing mechanics, not business news. Carried: Zacks raised its Q3 2026 EPS estimate to $0.21 (from $0.20) on Oct 1, Hold rating, FY2026 consensus $1.17; Q2 beat ($0.31 vs $0.28) on $342.15M revenue; $600M private placement of 6.75% senior notes due 2035. The weekend oil whipsaw (WTI ~$91 Friday, Brent >$103 after the Aramco attack) is the main sector read-through to watch into the debut.

watch_next: Does the premarket red deepen — the 10Y at 5.26% early Monday vs Thursday's 24-year high ~5.35%; a re-attack on the high pressures the bid.
Wednesday: FOMC minutes, plus the Fed speaker slate (Logan's +50bp call Thursday, Hammack's inflationary-mindset warning) — the week's main tape-mover after the jobs print.
Oil: G7 100M-barrel release implementation vs talk, Hormuz status, Aramco refinery-attack fallout — the swing macro input for yields.
Confirmation or denial of the FT Amazon-$8B-chip and Bloomberg Broadcom-$60B-Anthropic stories — the unresolved single-source swing factors.
Meta: timing of Judge Mathew's penalty ruling later this month on the now-confirmed $35-40B ask.
USAC: TXSE debut today — first session on the new exchange; venue move, not a business change.
